paragraphs: Here's what I want you to carry out of this passage, friend. Paul puts our present sufferings on one side and the glory to come on the other, and he says they are "not comparable" (Romans 8:18). He doesn't say the suffering isn't real, because the whole creation is groaning right along with us (Romans 8:22). He says the glory is so much bigger that the two don't even belong on the same scale.

So what do we do while we wait? Paul says that if we hope for what we do not yet see, we wait for it "patiently" (Romans 8:25). And when we're too worn out to even pray, the Spirit helps us in our weakness and intercedes for us "with groans too deep for words" (Romans 8:26). Friend, I spent years in the back of a junk drawer not knowing how to pray, and I promise you were never left talking to the ceiling.

Then Paul gives the firmest ground of all: "God works all things together for the good of those who love Him, who are called according to His purpose" (Romans 8:28). That means ALL things, not just the batches that come out pretty. The chain he lays out ends in glory: those He justified, "He also glorified" (Romans 8:30). So when the waiting gets heavy, baker, remember the One holding the chain has not dropped a single link.
